clue.text: Passion corporal displayed for dance

parts.note: a flame is a burning passion, as in an old flame
a corporal is a non-commissioned officer, NCO

explanation.surface: An army corporal shows his fiery side on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed for' just links the pieces to the definition. NCO stands for non-commissioned officer, the rank group a corporal belongs to.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamenco is a fiery Spanish style of dancing from Andalusia.

clue.text: Though surrounded by sea food, a large number starve

indicators.note: surrounded by means the A and M go inside the seafood word

parts.note: fish is food from the sea
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a large number

explanation.surface: Despite plenty of fish, crowds go hungry.
explanation.definitionFit: To famish is to make or become extremely hungry, to go without food.

clue.text: Admitted to be a gourmand's vice

parts.note: a gourmand is a glutton, whose vice is greed

explanation.surface: Gluttony is conceded to be a foodie's sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Admitted in the sense of conceded or accepted as true.

clue.text: Tempted to deliver yorker in consequence

indicators.note: in means the cricket word is placed inside the word for consequence

parts.note: an end is a result or consequence
tice is an old cricket term for a yorker, a ball pitched at the batsman's feet

explanation.surface: A bowler is tempted to bowl a yorker as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: A yorker is a cricket delivery aimed at the batsman's toes; TICE is its old name, which few solvers know. 'to deliver' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Enticed means lured or attracted with a promise of reward.

clue.text: Made concessions when jeopardised by scandal

explanation.definitionFit: To compromise is both to settle by mutual concession and to expose reputation to danger, as a scandal does.

clue.text: Apprehensive about Anglo-French assault

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for Anglo
a raid is a sudden assault or attack

explanation.surface: Nervous talk about a joint Anglo-French military attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link word here, attaching the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fearful or anxious about what may happen is to be apprehensive.

clue.text: A sweet and kindly disposed worker

parts.note: fond means affectionate or kindly disposed
an ant is the classic crossword worker, the worker ant

explanation.surface: A treat is offered by a friendly employee.
explanation.definitionFit: Fondant is a soft creamy confection used in sweets and icing.

clue.text: A woman in Minnesota?

indicators.note: in means the woman's name is put inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: MN is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Minnesota
Erica is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Asking about a lady living in a Midwest state.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a woman in a US state is a US citizen.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone living in a US state such as Minnesota is a citizen of the United States.

clue.text: Ten diets produced by small eateries

indicators.note: produced by suggests the letters of ten diets are rearranged to make something new

explanation.surface: Restaurants offering ten diet menus.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinette is a small dining area or alcove, a little place to eat.

clue.text: French husband wants season by the sea

parts.note: mari is the French word for husband
a season is a time, as in harvest time

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's spouse fancies a seaside holiday season.
explanation.definitionFit: Maritime describes things near or connected with the sea, as in coastal provinces.

clue.text: During winter no-one is put in prison

indicators.note: during tells us the answer sits inside the run of words winter no-one

explanation.surface: A grim note that nobody gets jailed throughout the cold months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'During' points to letters within 'winter no-one', ignoring the space and hyphen.
explanation.definitionFit: To intern someone is to confine them, especially in wartime, without trial.

clue.text: Sister invests money to get a jacket

indicators.note: invests in the sense of clothing or surrounding, so the sister's letters enclose the money

parts.note: pence is British money, pennies

explanation.surface: A nun puts her money into a new piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invests' looks financial, but here it means clothes or wraps round. A spencer is a short close-fitting jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A spencer is a short waist-length coat, named after an Earl Spencer.

clue.text: About to confront a lean, pragmatic man

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
to list is to lean to one side, as a ship does

explanation.surface: A practical person squares up to a thin opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to confront' only says the pieces stand face to face in sequence; it adds no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist is someone who deals with things as they are, a practical sort.

clue.text: Wagnerian-opera principals who foment sedition

parts.note: Wagner's Ring cycle is his famous four-part opera
principals are leaders, chief figures

explanation.surface: Lead singers in a Wagner work are rebels.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a relative clause, standing for people who stir up revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringleaders are the instigators who lead others into mischief or revolt.

clue.text: Show how to mount a public protest

explanation.definitionFit: To demonstrate is both to explain by showing how something works and to take part in a public protest march.

clue.text: Emergency take-off during motorcycle rally

explanation.definitionFit: A scramble is an urgent launch of fighter aircraft and also an off-road motorbike race.

clue.text: Foul-mouthed auditor not all regard as frightening

indicators.note: mouthed points to the mouth, or front, of the word foul, its first letter

parts.note: an ear is an auditor, the organ that listens
some means not all

explanation.surface: A sweary listener is regarded as menacing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foul-mouthed' looks like swearing, but the mouth of 'Foul' is its first letter. 'regard as' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearsome means alarming or terrifying in appearance.

clue.text: Dish fit for an emperor?

parts.note: playful reading: a dish named after a Roman emperor, as if made for one, though it is really a salad named after a restaurateur

explanation.definitionFit: This salad of romaine lettuce and croutons bears the name of the Roman ruler's title.

clue.text: A coach I have found to be insulting

parts.note: a coach is a bus
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: A trainer is found to be rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' looks like a trainer, but it is a long-distance bus. 'found to be' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Abusive means offensive or rude in language.

clue.text: Tramp leaves city paper in dehumidifier

indicators.note: in means the newspaper initials are placed inside the drying device

parts.note: a drier removes moisture, as a dehumidifier does
FT, the Financial Times, is the City of London's newspaper

explanation.surface: A vagrant leaves a newspaper in a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, so its paper is the Financial Times. 'leaves' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A drifter is a homeless wanderer, a vagrant.

clue.text: Hastings has a maze of small streets

explanation.definitionFit: Warren Hastings was the first governor-general of British India; the word also means a crowded network of passages.

clue.text: Public library on the border needs security

parts.note: P is an abbreviation for public
L is an abbreviation for library
an edge is a border

explanation.surface: A library on a frontier needs protection.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledge is something given as security for a loan, a guarantee.

clue.text: Silver circlet found on the rocks

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a circlet is a ring or round

explanation.surface: A silver ring is discovered among the rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' just links. 'on the rocks' looks like it describes where the ring was found, but it is the definition, as a stranded ship is.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel stuck on rocks or a sandbank has run ashore.

clue.text: Huge trouble pursues a lady's maid

indicators.note: pursues means the following pieces come after the letter A

parts.note: huge means big
to ail is to trouble, as in what ails you

explanation.surface: Great difficulty follows a lady's domestic servant.
explanation.walkthrough: An abigail is an old word for a lady's maid, from a character in a 17th-century play.
explanation.definitionFit: Abigail became a generic name for a waiting-woman or personal servant.

clue.text: Bibliophilic accountant!

parts.note: read as a book-loving bookkeeper, but it really means someone who keeps a book on bets at the races

explanation.definitionFit: A bookmaker takes bets and keeps a record of the odds, called making a book.

clue.text: Looked warily round street after being molested

indicators.note: round means the first word's letters go around the street abbreviation

parts.note: peered means looked closely or cautiously

explanation.surface: Someone eyed the road nervously after being assaulted.
explanation.definitionFit: To be pestered is to be harassed or bothered repeatedly.

clue.text: The Spanish still need to form a team

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
even means still, as in even better or still better

explanation.surface: Spaniards still have to assemble a side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'need to form a' just links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket side has eleven players, so the number names the side.

clue.text: Drive off to get English rum

parts.note: rum is British informal for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Getting English rum is a reason to drive away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink, but here it is the old British adjective meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate or push someone away emotionally, causing distance in a relationship.
